result.new_evidence_interpretation: The triangle readout reduced TRAIN CE from .34476 to .32694, yet raised VALID CE from .62986 to .63427 and lowered positive-39 Macro F1 from .51647 to .50280. The role-sign control also lost to native. The return-circuit study and the PPT witness give no affirmative task evidence for their proposed mechanisms. The original shuffle result leaves a more specific question open: does it matter which occurrence of the same wordpiece receives a relation’s attention, once the wordpiece’s total weight and each occurrence’s overall salience are held fixed?
result.one_hypothesis: On natural sentences containing two occurrences of an identical token ID with identical role bits, the native head gains decision accuracy from assigning attention between those occurrences differently for different relations and sentences. Part of that gain should survive a control that already knows each relation’s usual earlier-versus-later preference for that token.
result.transfer_and_substance: Use the fixed-margin comparison from contingency-table analysis. Treat the 40 relations as rows and the two occurrences as columns. Keep both margins of the observed table. This preserves how much each relation attends to the repeated token in total, and how much attention each occurrence attracts across all relations. The experiment removes only the sentence-specific part of who attends where, relative to a TRAIN-derived reference. A decision loss would locate a contribution inside lexical identity and entity role, at a finer resolution than the accepted unrestricted shuffle.
result.theory: For relation r, let m_r = α_r1 + α_r2 and x_r = α_r1/m_r, with occurrence 1 earlier. EPS makes 0 < x_r < 1. Estimate a reference earlier-occurrence fraction q_r on TRAIN for the same token ID and role bits. On each VALID pair set x′_r = sigmoid(logit(q_r) + h), where the single h solves Σ_r m_r x′_r = Σ_r m_r x_r. The left side increases continuously from zero to Σ_r m_r, so the solution exists and is unique. This is the minimizer of Σ_r m_r KL(Bern(x′_r) || Bern(q_r)) under the column constraint, by differentiation. The native-minus-control logit change is exactly Σ_pairs m_r(x_r − x′_r)(u_r1 − u_r2). Thus even large redistributions disappear at the decoder when the occurrence values agree. The missing observable is a net gain in correct natural decisions from this residual alignment. The projection is standard mathematics. The strongest competing explanation for a positive result is a relation-specific positional rule, such as preferring the occurrence nearest the subject, that varies across sentences with the same lexical key. That rule would pass this test. Semantic disambiguation would remain unresolved.

minimal_test.input: Use the frozen seed13 checkpoint, first 8192 TRAIN examples in stored order, and all 19584 exposed VALID examples. Read native normalized attention, token IDs, role bits, valid-token masks, decoded token values and biases. Use labels only to score VALID.
minimal_test.intervention: For each supported repeated pair, replace its two weights by m_r x′_r and m_r(1−x′_r) for every relation. Apply the replacement simultaneously to all supported pairs in the sentence. All other weights are copied. For each TRAIN key and relation, set q_r = (0.5 + Σ x_r)/(1 + N), where N counts qualifying TRAIN pairs for that key. This estimates occurrence preference from native attention without fitting labels or a second classifier.
minimal_test.fixed_selection: A pair consists of exactly two valid, non-special positions with the same (token ID, four role bits) within one sentence. Use every key with N ≥ 32 on TRAIN. Position order breaks the symmetry. A VALID sentence is eligible if it has at least one supported pair. Include every eligible sentence, regardless of label, native correctness or attention magnitude. Require at least 1000 eligible VALID sentences, including at least 250 with a positive gold relation.
minimal_test.budget: One forward collection per split, one TRAIN aggregation, one counterfactual VALID replay. Solve h by float64 scalar bisection. Zero optimizer updates, TEST reads or COS writes.
minimal_test.metric: On the same eligible sentences compute mean CE(control) − CE(native) and accuracy(native) − accuracy(control), counting both directions of decision flips. Also report coverage, flip counts, and the two differences across all VALID, where ineligible sentences contribute zero paired difference.
minimal_test.pass: Require the coverage floors, eligible-set CE difference ≥ 0.005 nats per example, and eligible-set accuracy difference ≥ 0.003 absolute. These are prospective feasibility thresholds on exposed VALID.
minimal_test.stop: Stop this hypothesis if coverage or either outcome misses its threshold. Freeze the lexical key, support floor, occurrence count, reference estimator, cohort and thresholds before collection. A pass earns a fixed-checkpoint mechanism result only.

result.why_distinct: This intervention operates downstream of the original Born scores at their existing decoder. It uses neither a new circuit nor an added predictive feature. The unrestricted shuffle can damage a model simply by moving attention between different words or entity roles. Both routes are unavailable here. The column constraint also protects sentence-specific salience shared across labels. The measured endpoint is the balance of correct decisions gained and lost, so a decoder-invisible change in attention cannot pass. No relation or example from the failed witness is targeted.
result.implementation_delta: Add one isolated evaluation plugin that groups positions, accumulates TRAIN fractions and replays VALID logits with the two weights replaced. Its affected-mechanism fixtures should check both margins to 1e−10 absolute, native-logit replay against the float64 reference to 1e−8, and agreement between the analytic logit change and direct replay to 1e−8. Treat a fixture failure as an invalid run.
result.claim_ceiling: A pass would show that, for this checkpoint and cohort, the native sentence-specific division of attention between repeated occurrences contributes to prediction beyond the specified lexical preference and salience control. Fixed-margin projection and conditional attention ablation are the nearest method risks. Novelty would depend on the task finding. Necessity against all positional rules or alternative trained heads, linkage to the accepted five-seed L4 gain, and a substantive L5 theory would remain open.
